summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for acute respiratory distress and found to have Pseudomonas pneumonia and recurrent C. difficile colitis. He was treated with IV cefepime for pneumonia and oral vancomycin for C. diff, with a PICC line placed for antibiotic administration. His respiratory status improved to baseline on 35% oxygen, and he remained afebrile with stable labs. Chronic issues including right leg pain, seizure disorder, and psychiatric conditions were managed with home medications. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics and an additional two weeks of oral vancomycin, with follow-up coordinated through his care team.
